Nu Holdings Ltd. NU suffered a political shock this week. Following Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil, its shares fell 16.95% on Oct. 26 to $12.59. The stock finished at $12.05 on Oct. 29, down 20.5% from Oct. 23.

Investors are reassessing Brazilian market risks. The Bovespa Index lost 13.9% on Oct. 26, and the real slid more than 10% against the dollar intraday. Questions about government spending and interest rates matter for Nu because Brazil accounts for most of its customers.

These market worries contrast with operating momentum. Nu generated nearly $5.9 billion in second-quarter 2026 gross revenues, a 39% currency-neutral increase, and $1.06 billion in net income. Its customer base reached 139 million, including roughly 118 million in Brazil. Continued expansion provides some support against economic pressures.

However, credit quality deserves attention. Loans overdue more than 90 days rose 35 basis points to 6.9% in the second quarter, even as earlier-stage delinquencies eased to 4.8%. Prolonged elevated interest rates could increase repayment difficulties, pushing credit losses higher and squeezing lending profitability.

Third-quarter results, tentatively expected on Nov. 12, will help investors assess whether the share-price decline reflects broader market fears or weakening fundamentals. Loan growth, financing costs, credit provisions and currency movements will be important indicators. Sustained operating growth could support a recovery, provided asset quality remains manageable.

Nu Holdings' Brazil Peers Face Credit and Currency Risks

MercadoLibre MELI faces Brazilian currency and credit risks through its Mercado Pago unit. MercadoLibre reported second-quarter 2026 payment volume of $101 billion, up 56%, while its credit portfolio exceeded $16 billion. MercadoLibre's lending expansion supports revenue growth, but Brazil's election uncertainty could increase defaults and pressure margins over coming quarters.

StoneCo STNE also faces Brazil's shifting interest-rate outlook and merchant credit risks. StoneCo's second-quarter 2026 credit portfolio reached R$3.75 billion, up 107.5% year over year, while provisions for expected credit losses increased. StoneCo's merchant-focused lending provides growth potential, although weaker business activity could raise defaults and further restrict lending profitability.

NU's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of NU have declined 16.6% over the past six months, underperforming the broader industry and the S&P 500 composite.

Michael Burry always gets attention with his stock picks and market calls. He became famous for betting against subprime mortgages before the 2008 crisis, and his fund Scion Capital reportedly returned over 480% from November 2000 to June 2008.

Burry closed his later fund, Scion Asset Management, in November 2025. He now shares his trades on a paid Substack called Cassandra Unchained. There are no official returns or 13F filings to check, so his calls can only be judged from his public posts and the bets reporters have tracked.

Burry is not the only big investor worried about AI. Billionaire Ray Dalio warns that AI has become a crowded trade, while Philippe Laffont of Coatue calls it a supercycle. See which AI stocks they own.

The crash calls that did not come

Burry has warned about a crash at least six times since 2021. In June 2021, he said the stock market was in the biggest speculative bubble ever and warned of "the mother of all crashes," Fortune reported. Fortune noted in July 2022 that his steady stream of doom predictions led some people to say he was crying wolf. Stocks did fall in 2022, and the S&P 500 had its worst first half since 1970. In May 2022, he said the index could sink as far as 1,862, Fortune reported, and it never came close.

In January 2023, he posted one word, "Sell," and in March he said he was "wrong to say sell," Business Insider reported. In August 2023, his fund's filings showed bearish positions against the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. The S&P 500 was already up nearly 16% for the year.

The calls keep coming. In April, he bought puts on the semiconductor ETF SOXX after chip stocks jumped 47% in 18 days, Bloomberg reported. In August, he wrote that it is "possible we are near a major top, and possible a 1987-type fall," CNBC reported. Burry also shorted Micron and called it "cyclical like no other," and Claude AI said his warning "deserves respect." Click to read the full list of Michael Burry's top 10 stock picks.

Methodology

We scanned credible media reports that covered Michael Burry's stock picks. Burry closed his fund, Scion Asset Management, in November 2025, so there are no 13F filings to check. He now shares his trades on his paid Substack, Cassandra Unchained. We used media reports that cite his Substack posts and reports by established news outlets that tracked his bets. We included only stocks that these reports tied to Burry's own comments or trades.

MercadoLibre (MELI) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Shares of this operator of an online marketplace and payments system in Latin America have returned -3.2% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.9% change. The Zacks Internet - Commerce industry, to which MercadoLibre belongs, has gained 1.3% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

While media releases or rumors about a substantial change in a company's business prospects usually make its stock 'trending' and lead to an immediate price change, there are always some fundamental facts that eventually dominate the buy-and-hold decision-making.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

MercadoLibre is expected to post earnings of $9.41 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +13.1%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.6%.

For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $38.09 points to a change of -3.3% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed -2.6%.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $55.19 indicates a change of +44.9% from what MercadoLibre is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -1.5%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, MercadoLibre is rated Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:

12 Month EPS
12-month consensus EPS estimate for MELI
Revenue Growth Forecast

Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.

In the case of MercadoLibre, the consensus sales estimate of $10.66 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +43.8%. The $41.74 billion and $53.98 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +44.5% and +29.3%, respectively.

Last Reported Results and Surprise History

MercadoLibre reported revenues of $10.17 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +49.8%. EPS of $9.19 for the same period compares with $10.31 a year ago.

Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.77 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +4.07%. The EPS surprise was +5.75%.

Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed EPS estimates just once. The company topped consensus revenue estimates each time over this period.

Valuation

No investment decision can be efficient without considering a stock's valuation. Whether a stock's current price rightly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects is an essential determinant of its future price performance.

While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.

The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.

MercadoLibre is graded C on this front, indicating that it is trading at par with its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Bottom Line

The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about MercadoLibre. However, its Zacks Rank #4 does suggest that it may underperform the broader market in the near term.

detail:
MercadoLibre (MELI) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
Zacks Equity Research

The market expects MercadoLibre (MELI) to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook is important in assessing the company's earnings picture, but a powerful factor that might influence its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This operator of an online marketplace and payments system in Latin America is expected to post quarterly earnings of $9.41 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +13.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $10.66 billion, up 43.8% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.62% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for MELI
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for MercadoLibre?

For MercadoLibre, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +4.93%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that MercadoLibre will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that MercadoLibre would post earnings of $8.69 per share when it actually produced earnings of $9.19, delivering a surprise of +5.75%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates just once.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. MercadoLibre doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

DoorDash vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool

As delivery networks expand globally, investors often weigh domestic leaders against international powerhouses. Choosing between DoorDash Inc. (NASDAQ:DASH) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI) requires understanding local commerce versus regional e-commerce dominance.

DoorDash dominates the U.S. food and grocery delivery landscape by connecting merchants with a vast courier network and proprietary commerce tools. MercadoLibre operates a massive e-commerce and fintech ecosystem across Latin America, serving millions of active users. Both companies are compared because they represent high-growth platforms leveraging logistics and digital payments to capture shifting consumer spending habits in their respective regions.

The case for DoorDash

DoorDash operates a local commerce platform connecting consumers, merchants, and couriers through a delivery and pickup network. The company serves various categories among retail stocks including grocery, pet, and convenience stores across more than 40 countries. It utilizes social-first marketing campaigns through its partnership with the agency Get Engaged and reported over 35 million members across its DashPass and Wolt+ subscription services at the end of 2025.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $13.7 billion, which was a growth of approximately 27.9% compared to the previous year. This revenue expansion supported a net income of roughly $935 million for the period, indicating a stronger bottom line. The result represents a substantial improvement from the net income of $123 million reported in FY 2024.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity. The current ratio is nearly 1.4x, while free cash flow, defined as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, reached roughly $2.2 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 43.2% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation because stock-based compensation is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates a vast digital ecosystem that integrates e-commerce marketplace services with the Mercado Pago fintech platform. The company serves a diverse range of 131 million unique buyers and small businesses across 18 countries in Latin America, including Brazil and Mexico. This model positions it uniquely by combining retail, logistics, and financial services in one integrated platform.

During FY 2025, revenue rose to about $28.9 billion, representing growth of approximately 39% over the prior year. The company generated net income of roughly $2.0 billion for the same period, which was an increase from the $1.9 billion earned in FY 2024. This performance resulted in a net margin of close to 6.9% for the fiscal year.

As of the December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 1.7x, which compares total debt against shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.2x, while free cash flow reached about $10.8 billion in FY 2025. Free cash flow is calculated by subtracting capital expenditures from cash generated by operating activities.

Risk profile comparison

DoorDash faces significant pressure from global and local delivery services like Delivery Hero (OTC:DLVHF) and Prosus (OTC:PROSF). The company also manages legal risks related to courier classification and $131.5 million in settlement costs arising from pay regulations. Operational risks include cybersecurity vulnerabilities, platform outages, and the complex task of managing rapid international expansion into new markets.

MercadoLibre operates in a highly competitive market against international players such as Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). The business is exposed to financial risks from high inflation and currency volatility across various Latin American markets. Regulatory changes regarding privacy laws and potential tax reforms also create uncertainty for its fintech and e-commerce operations.

Valuation comparison

MercadoLibre appears to be the more attractively valued option as it trades at a lower multiple of both sales and future earnings estimates. A Forward P/E compares the share price to future earnings estimates for the next year. The P/S ratio measures the market value of the company relative to its sales over the past twelve months.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

MercadoLibre evolved from the 'eBay of Latin America' to something more akin to a combination of Amazon and PayPal Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL). In 2025, the company made large investments in its Brazilian logistics network, cut down the free-shipping threshold in Brazil in June, and nearly doubled its consumer loan book. This drove impressive growth for the company and investors, with an increasing focus on financial services over delivering goods.

Yet the immediate concern with left-of-center Luis Lula winning the Brazilian presidential election is that the new administration will start addressing Brazil's high government and consumer debt levels, which will keep interest rates there around their current very high levels. That's bad for a consumer-loan-focused business like MercadoLibre, and shares have been hammered this week as a result.

Long-term, however, such fears are probably overblown. In fact, in the current fiscal year, revenue is expected to jump 45% to $41.9 billion, with slightly higher free cash flow and slightly lower net income. Overall, it's a good picture for MercadoLibre.

Things look good for DoorDash, as well. Originally a prepared-food delivery service, DoorDash has been finding success by expanding into new business verticals, such as delivering electronics, apparel, and groceries. Groceries, in particular, are expected to grow twice as fast as meal delivery for the company in the coming years. International expansion, wth the acquisition of the U.K. based Deliveroo, is helping the company expand as well. Advances in efficiency and speed, and improvements that help customers build order carts in the app, are improving sales, too.

For the current fiscal year, 2026, revenue is expected to rise 30% to $17.8 billion, with net income improving about 20% to $1.13 billion.

The stocks of each of these businesses are priced as high-growth stocks, as shown by their high forward P/E ratios. The investment decision here is driven by the markets where their core customers are less likely to be affected by rising debt levels and lowering consumer confidence. Both face those issues, but the U.S. market that is core to DoorDash's business historically holds up better than Latin America when economic times get tough. In 2026, go with DoorDash.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

Walmart Inc. WMT and MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI are strengthening their competitive positions through digital innovation, expanding customer engagement and investments in their respective ecosystems. With evolving consumer preferences, technological advancements and profitability trends shaping their growth trajectories, a closer assessment of their fundamentals, earnings expectations and valuations can help identify the more promising investment opportunity.

Walmart, with a market cap of around $949.6 billion, is a global omnichannel retail giant with an extensive store network and a growing digital ecosystem spanning e-commerce, advertising, marketplace, membership and fulfillment services. Its scale, price leadership and expanding higher-margin businesses support its long-term growth prospects.

MercadoLibre is a leading e-commerce and fintech platform in Latin America, operating an integrated ecosystem across online commerce, payments, credit, advertising and financial services. Its expanding logistics infrastructure, Mercado Pago adoption and technology-driven initiatives provide multiple avenues for growth. The company currently has a market cap of $85.2 billion.

The Case for Walmart

Walmart's growth prospects are supported by its extensive retail network, competitive pricing and strengthening omnichannel capabilities. Its broad merchandise assortment and focus on affordability continue to attract shoppers across income groups, supporting customer traffic and market share gains. The company's vast store footprint also provides a strategic fulfillment advantage, enabling faster deliveries and greater shopping convenience.

Digital transformation remains a key growth catalyst. Walmart continues to benefit from growing e-commerce penetration, marketplace expansion and improved fulfillment capabilities. Faster delivery services are encouraging repeat purchases and strengthening customer engagement, supporting Walmart+ membership adoption. The company's ability to leverage stores for online order fulfillment also provides opportunities to improve delivery economics.

Its evolving business mix is another upside. Higher-margin revenue streams, including advertising, membership, marketplace services and data solutions, are becoming increasingly important contributors. These businesses, alongside supply-chain automation and improving delivery efficiency, are supporting e-commerce profitability. Walmart is also extending its digital platforms and membership offerings across international markets, creating additional opportunities for operational efficiencies and scalability.

Nevertheless, pharmacy-related deflation, rising healthcare and claims costs, higher depreciation expenses and continued investments in pricing and customer experience remain concerns. These factors could constrain near-term margin expansion. Despite such challenges, Walmart's resilient retail operations, growing digital ecosystem and improving business mix remain encouraging. Management's raised fiscal 2027 outlook on its second-quarter earnings call further reinforces confidence in its growth trajectory.
